questions.funFact: The 50 stars represent the 50 states and the 13 stripes represent the original colonies.
The Union Jack combines three crosses: St. George (England), St. Andrew (Scotland), and St. Patrick (Ireland).
The French tricolor was adopted during the Revolution of 1789 and inspired countless other national flags worldwide.
The black-red-gold tricolor dates back to the Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 and the German unification movement.
The Italian tricolor was inspired by the French flag and first used by Napoleon's Cispadane Republic in 1797.
Spain's red and yellow colors date back to the 18th century when Charles III needed a flag visible at sea.
Japan's flag is called 'Nisshōki' (sun flag) or 'Hinomaru' (circle of the sun) — one of the world's simplest and most recognizable.
The large star represents the Communist Party and the four smaller stars represent the four social classes of China.
Brazil's flag shows the night sky over Rio de Janeiro on November 15, 1889 — the day the republic was proclaimed.
Australia's flag features the Southern Cross constellation and the Union Jack, reflecting its ties to Britain.
Canada's maple leaf flag was adopted in 1965 after a passionate national debate nicknamed the 'Great Canadian Flag Debate'.
Peter the Great modeled Russia's tricolor on the Dutch flag after visiting the Netherlands in 1697.
The blue Ashoka Chakra (wheel of dharma) in the center has 24 spokes representing the 24 hours in a day.
Turkey's crescent and star design is one of the oldest flag symbols, dating back to the Ottoman Empire's 14th century.
Mexico's coat of arms depicts an eagle eating a serpent on a cactus — the Aztec founding myth of Tenochtitlan.
The sun on Argentina's flag is called the 'Sun of May' commemorating the May Revolution of 1810.
South Korea's Taegukgi features Taoist symbols: the yin-yang circle and four trigrams representing heaven, earth, water, and fire.
Saudi Arabia is one of few countries with Arabic script on its flag. The text is the Islamic declaration of faith (Shahada).
South Africa's six-color flag was adopted in 1994 to symbolize the converging paths of the diverse population.
Nigeria's green and white bicolor was designed by 23-year-old Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi who won a national competition in 1959.
Egypt's Eagle of Saladin in the center is named after the legendary 12th-century sultan who defeated the Crusaders.
The nine stripes on Greece's flag represent the nine syllables of the Greek phrase 'Freedom or Death' (Ελευθερία ή Θάνατος).
Portugal's armillary sphere on the flag represents the Age of Discovery when Portuguese explorers mapped the world.
Sweden's Nordic cross design is the oldest continuously used national flag design, adopted around 1663.
Norway's flag contains the flags of Iceland, Finland, Denmark, and Sweden hidden within its design.
The Danish Dannebrog is the world's oldest national flag still in use, allegedly falling from the sky during a 1219 battle in Estonia.
The Netherlands' orange-white-blue Prince's Flag was the world's first tricolor and inspired the French Revolution flag.
Belgium's vertical tricolor was inspired by the 1789 Brabant Revolution against Austrian rule.
Switzerland has one of the only two square national flags in the world, along with Vatican City.
Austria's red-white-red design is one of the oldest heraldic coats of arms in the world, dating to the 13th century.
Poland's white represents peace and the red represents courage — simple but deeply meaningful to a nation that has survived great adversity.
Czechia kept Czechoslovakia's old flag after the peaceful 1993 Velvet Divorce, while Slovakia designed a new one.
Hungary's tricolor was first used during the 1848 revolution against Habsburg rule.
Romania and Chad have nearly identical flags — both use blue, yellow, and red vertical stripes.
Bulgaria's green stripe was added after the Liberation from Ottoman rule in 1878 to represent freedom and hope.
Croatia's shield features the distinctive red-and-white checkerboard (šahovnica) pattern that dates back to medieval times.
Finland's blue cross on white represents the blue lakes and white snow of the Finnish landscape.
Ireland's tricolor represents the Catholics (green), Protestants (orange), and peace between them (white).
Ukraine's blue and yellow represent blue sky above golden wheat fields — the nation's agricultural heartland.
Iceland's flag is the reverse of the Norwegian flag — red-and-white cross on blue, representing fire and ice.
Estonia's blue, black, and white tricolor symbolizes sky and sea, the dark past, and future hope.
Latvia's dark red (carmine) bicolor is one of the world's oldest flag designs, described in a 1279 Latvian chronicle.
Lithuania's yellow, green, and red tricolor was adopted in 1918 and readopted in 1989 when independence was restored.
Slovakia's flag adds the double-barred cross on the Tatra Mountains to distinguish it from Slovenia and Russia's similar flags.
Slovenia's coat of arms shows Mount Triglav (the national symbol), three stars, and undulating blue lines for rivers.
Serbia's flag uses the Pan-Slavic colors red, blue, and white, with a royal coat of arms added to distinguish it.
Indonesia's 'Sang Saka Merah Putih' flag is identical to Monaco's — both use the same red-over-white design.
Pakistan's green represents Islam while the white stripe represents the religious minorities in the country.
Bangladesh's red circle is slightly off-center so it appears centered when the flag flies in the wind.
The Philippines' flag is unique — it's flown upside down (red on top) during wartime as a war flag.
Vietnam's golden star represents the five main classes of people: workers, peasants, intellectuals, merchants, and soldiers.
Thailand's current flag was designed in 1917 by King Vajiravudh, who said 'Nations are but stripes of cloth'.
Malaysia's 14-stripe flag represents the 13 states and federal territories, inspired by the American flag.
Singapore's five stars represent democracy, peace, progress, justice, and equality. The crescent moon represents a young nation.
New Zealand has considered changing its flag multiple times to distinguish it from Australia's nearly identical design.
Peru's coat of arms features a vicuña (a relative of the llama), a cinchona tree (source of quinine), and a cornucopia.
Colombia's yellow represents gold, blue the seas, and red the blood of patriots — designed by Francisco de Miranda.
Chile's star is called the 'lone star' (La Estrella Solitaria) and the blue represents the sky, white the Andes snow.
Venezuela's eight stars represent the eight original provinces that signed the Act of Independence in 1811.
Ecuador's coat of arms features a condor, Chimborazo volcano (highest point from Earth's center), and a ship.
Bolivia is one of the few countries with two capitals: Sucre (constitutional) and La Paz (seat of government).
Paraguay is unique in having different emblems on each side of the flag — the only country whose flag differs front and back.
Uruguay's Sun of May (same as Argentina's) honors the May Revolution of 1810 that began South American independence.
Cuba's flag was designed in 1848 by Cuban exiles in New York — the lone star represents Cuba's independence.
Jamaica is one of only two countries whose flag contains neither red, white, nor blue — the other is Mauritania.
The Dominican Republic's flag is the only national flag featuring a Bible, specifically opened to the Gospel of John.
Iran's flag features the 'Allah' symbol in the center and the phrase 'God is Great' repeated 22 times along the borders.
Iraq's flag has changed its center inscription multiple times, currently showing 'God is Great' in Arabic.
Israel's flag is based on the traditional Jewish prayer shawl (tallit) with the Star of David (Magen David) in the center.
Jordan's flag features a seven-pointed star representing the seven verses of Al-Fatiha (opening chapter of the Quran).
Lebanon's cedar tree (arz il-rabb) is a symbol of immortality and steadiness mentioned 77 times in the Old Testament.
Syria's two green stars represent Syria and Egypt — remnants of the brief United Arab Republic union (1958–1961).
The UAE's four Pan-Arab colors represent the Arab world's unity — the vertical red stripe was chosen to bind the colors.
Kuwait's black trapezoid is unique among Gulf state flags and represents the black oil on which Kuwait's wealth was built.
Qatar's maroon color was created by the local climate fading the original red flag — they adopted the faded color officially!
Bahrain's five white triangles represent the five pillars of Islam; it's the only flag with five points on a serrated edge.
Oman's national emblem shows crossed khanjar daggers and a sword — traditional symbols of Omani identity.
Yemen uses the Pan-Arab colors without any additional emblems — a simple yet historic tricolor.
Afghanistan has changed its flag more than any other country in modern times — over 18 different flags since 1900.
Ethiopia's flag colors inspired the Pan-African color scheme used by many post-colonial nations across Africa.
Kenya's flag features a Maasai shield and two crossed spears, representing the defense of the country.
Tanzania's diagonal design combines elements from Tanganyika and Zanzibar flags after their 1964 union.
Uganda's flag features the Grey Crowned Crane, the national bird known for its graceful dancing displays.
Morocco's green pentagram (Seal of Solomon) is the only flag with a five-pointed star outline rather than a solid star.
Algeria's flag was designed in 1954 by Messali Hadj's nationalist movement during the war for independence from France.
Tunisia's red crescent and star design dates back to 1831 when Husseinid Bey added it to the Ottoman-style red background.
Libya's current flag was restored in 2011 after Gaddafi's all-green flag was removed following the civil war.
Sudan's green triangle represents Islam and prosperity — added to the Pan-Arab tricolor upon independence in 1956.
Somalia's five-pointed star represents the five regions historically inhabited by Somali people.
Ghana's black star in 1957 was the first Pan-African black star on a flag, inspiring Jamaica, Guinea-Bissau and others.
Côte d'Ivoire's tricolor is the reverse of Ireland's flag — orange, white, and green from left to right.
Senegal's green star was added to distinguish it from Mali's otherwise identical flag after their federation dissolved.
Cameroon's yellow star replaced the two stars that used to represent the French and British regions of the country.
Mozambique is the only country with an AK-47 on its flag — representing defense of the nation.
Zimbabwe's Zimbabwe Bird is based on carved soapstone figures found at Great Zimbabwe ruins — an ancient stone city.
Uzbekistan's 12 stars represent the months of the year and the crescent moon represents the Islamic faith.
Kazakhstan's sky-blue flag features a steppe eagle and a sun with 32 rays representing prosperity.
Azerbaijan's flag uses three equal horizontal stripes — blue for the Turkic heritage, red for modernization, and green for Islam.
Armenia's red represents the blood spilled defending the homeland, blue the sky, and orange the creative talent of Armenians.
Georgia's Five Cross Flag (Bolnisi Cross) is one of the oldest national flags, dating to the 5th century AD.
Belarus's ornamental red-and-white stripe on the left is based on a traditional folk pattern from the Belarusian village of Kostyanyets.
Moldova's coat of arms features a Moldavian auroch's head — the extinct wild cattle that once roamed the region.
Montenegro's golden eagle on the flag is derived from the coat of arms of the Petrović-Njegoš dynasty that ruled for centuries.
North Macedonia's 'Sun of Vergina' design was changed in 1995 after a dispute with Greece over its historical symbolism.
Albania's double-headed eagle dates back to 1443 when national hero Skanderbeg used it as his military seal.
Bosnia's flag was imposed by the international community in 1998 — it's the only UN member flag chosen by an international body.
Kosovo's 2008 flag is one of the newest in the world; it shows the country's map in gold on blue.
Taiwan's 'white sun in blue sky' flag originated with the Chinese Nationalist Party (Kuomintang) in 1895.
Palestine's flag uses Pan-Arab colors of black, white, green, and red — representing the Arab Revolt of 1916.
North Korea's flag features a red star symbolizing communism, flanked by white borders representing purity.
Myanmar's three-stripe flag with a white star replaced the socialist-era peacock flag when the military renamed the country.
Cambodia is one of few countries featuring a building on its flag — the Angkor Wat temple complex, built in the 12th century.
Laos is the only communist country without a red star on its flag — the white circle represents the full moon over the Mekong River.
Mongolia's Soyombo symbol represents fire, sun, moon, earth, water, and yin-yang — a profound Buddhist symbol.
Nepal is the only country in the world with a non-rectangular national flag — it's formed by two stacked triangular pennants.
Sri Lanka's golden lion holding a sword is the symbol of the Sinhala people; the four leaves represent Buddhism.
The Maldives' crescent moon and the green field represent Islam and the green tropical landscape of the islands.
Bhutan's Thunder Dragon (Druk) gives the country its own name — Druk Yul (Land of the Thunder Dragon).
Brunei's crest features a crescent moon (Islam), a parasol (monarchy), wings (justice), and hands cupped in prayer.
Timor-Leste became independent in 2002 — its flag's black triangle symbolizes the dark colonial past and the white the future.
PNG's bird of paradise (raggiana) and Southern Cross were designed by a 15-year-old girl who won a national competition in 1971.
Fiji's unique light blue shade sets it apart from other blue flags and was chosen to represent the Pacific Ocean.
Solomon Islands' five stars represent the five main island groups of the archipelago.
Vanuatu's boar tusk and fern leaf represent peace and the Melanesian way of life (kastom).
Samoa's flag added a fifth star to the Southern Cross in 1949, unlike other Pacific nations that kept four.
Tonga's constitution enshrines the red cross on its flag — it cannot be altered or removed by law.
Kiribati's rising sun and frigate bird represent Kiribati's position near the International Date Line — the first to see each new day.
The Marshall Islands' flag has two diagonal stripes and a 24-pointed star — the stripes represent the Ratak and Ralik island chains.
Micronesia's four stars represent the four main island groups: Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Yap.
Palau's golden circle is slightly off-center to avoid looking like Japan's flag — it represents the full moon.
Nauru's flag is a literal map — the white star represents the island positioned one degree south of the equator (gold line).
Tuvalu's nine stars represent its nine islands; after independence some were removed and then restored after a political controversy.
Rwanda redesigned its flag in 2001 to break from the association with the 1994 genocide and embrace a new vision.
Burundi's three stars represent the three ethnic groups: Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa — a symbol of unity after civil war.
The DR Congo's sky-blue field with a diagonal red stripe was designed to represent blood, fire, and national dignity.
The Republic of Congo's diagonal stripe design was inspired by Africa's first independent republic flag — Ghana.
The Central African Republic's vertical red stripe uniting all horizontal bands symbolizes national blood and sacrifice.
Chad and Romania have nearly identical flags — Chad claims priority but both countries use the same blue, yellow, red tricolor.
Niger's orange disc in the white stripe represents the sun and the country's Saharan desert.
Mali's flag was originally green-gold-red with a black human figure (kanaga), which was removed in 1961.
Burkina Faso means 'Land of Upright People' in Mòoré and Dyula — its red, green, and gold mirror Pan-African colors.
Guinea's tricolor is the reverse of France's flag — a deliberate statement of anti-colonialism upon independence in 1958.
Guinea-Bissau's black star was inspired by Ghana's — representing the African continent and its people.
Sierra Leone's green, white, and blue represent agriculture, unity, and the Atlantic Ocean respectively.
Liberia's flag is closely modeled on the United States flag — it was founded by freed American slaves in 1847.
Togo's five horizontal stripes represent the five administrative regions. The red square and white star stand for solidarity.
Benin briefly changed its flag to a plain green one during the Marxist era (1975–1990) before restoring the original.
Gabon's yellow stripe represents the equator that runs through the country; the blue is the Atlantic Ocean.
Equatorial Guinea's coat of arms features a silk-cotton tree (God Tree) under which a treaty was signed in 1778.
São Tomé and Príncipe's two black stars represent the two main islands. The country sits right on the equator.
Cape Verde's circle of 10 yellow stars represents the 10 main islands of the archipelago.
Mauritania added two red stripes in 2017 — representing the blood Mauritanians are ready to shed defending the country.
Djibouti's light blue represents the Issa (Somali) people, green the Afar people, and the red star symbolizes unity and blood.
Eritrea's olive wreath with 30 leaves represents the 30 years of struggle for independence from Ethiopia (1961–1991).
South Sudan became the world's newest internationally recognized country on July 9, 2011, after decades of civil war.
Madagascar's white and red represent the Merina (highland people) and the green represents the coastal people.
Zambia's fish eagle in flight represents the freedom of the people while the red stands for the nation's resources.
Haiti's flag was created when Jean-Jacques Dessalines ripped the white from a French tricolor in 1803, creating blue and red.
Trinidad and Tobago's black stripe represents Earth, the red represents fire and the sun, and white represents water.
Barbados' broken trident symbolizes the break from its colonial past — a full trident appears on the old British colonial badge.
The Bahamas' aquamarine and gold represent the sea and sandy beaches; the black triangle symbolizes the unity of the people.
Saint Lucia's twin triangles represent the Pitons — two volcanic plugs that are the island's most recognizable landmarks.
Saint Vincent's three diamonds form a 'V' for Vincent — the only national flag to contain a 'V' shape.
The rising sun on Antigua's flag represents the dawn of a new era; the black symbolizes the African heritage of its people.
Grenada's nutmeg on the flag reflects the island's history as the world's second-largest producer of nutmeg.
The two stars on Saint Kitts' flag represent the two islands, while the black stripe stands for the African heritage.
Belize has the only national flag with people on it — two men (a mestizo and a Creole) holding a mahogany shield.
Guatemala's quetzal bird is one of the most revered symbols in Mesoamerica; Mayan kings wore quetzal feathers as crowns.
Honduras's five stars represent the five former Central American Federation nations that once formed a single country.
Costa Rica's flag was inspired by the French tricolor to honor the ideals of the French Revolution.
Panama's four quarters represent the Liberal (red) and Conservative (blue) parties, separated by white for peace.
El Salvador's coat of arms features five volcanoes representing the five Central American nations and the ocean between them.
Nicaragua's coat of arms features the same five volcanoes as El Salvador — both belong to the former Central American Federation.
Suriname's golden star represents unity between its five main ethnic groups: Creoles, Hindustani, Javanese, Maroons, and Amerindians.
Guyana's flag is called the 'Golden Arrowhead' — the golden arrow points to the country's bright future.
Malta's George Cross was awarded by King George VI for the island's bravery during the WWII Siege of Malta.
Cyprus is one of only two countries with a map on their flag (along with Kosovo) — the copper-colored island represents the Greek name Kypros.
Luxembourg's flag is almost identical to the Netherlands' but uses a lighter shade of blue (azure vs. cobalt).
Monaco's red-over-white flag is identical to Indonesia's — the tiny principality's colors come from the Grimaldi family crest.
Liechtenstein discovered at the 1936 Olympics that its flag was identical to Haiti's — it added a crown to distinguish itself.
Andorra is a co-principality ruled jointly by the President of France and the Bishop of Urgell, Spain.
San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving sovereign state and constitutional republic, founded in 301 AD.
Vatican City is the world's smallest country and the only one with a square flag alongside Switzerland.
Kyrgyzstan's tunduk symbol represents the crown of the traditional Kyrgyz yurt (portable felt tent).
Tajikistan's crown and seven stars represent the Tajik people and the seven families of Tajikistan.
Turkmenistan's flag has the most complex design of any national flag — five carpet motifs representing the five major tribes.
Malawi briefly changed its flag under President Mutharika in 2010–2012, adding a full sun, before reverting to the original rising sun.
Lesotho's Basotho hat (mokorotlo) replaced a spear and weapons symbol in 2006 — a move toward peaceful symbolism.
Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) renamed itself in 2018 to use the Swati name — the flag features a Nguni shield and spears.
Comoros' four stars and four stripes represent the four main islands: Ngazidja, Ndzuwani, Mwali, and Mayotte.
Mauritius has the only four-horizontal-stripe flag in the world — the stripes represent the Indian Ocean, independence, agriculture, and unity.
Seychelles' five radiating stripes represent the five political parties that came together at independence in 1977.
Gambia's blue stripe represents the Gambia River, which the entire country is built around — it flows from east to west.
Namibia's golden sun represents life and energy; the flag was adopted at independence in 1990 from South Africa.
Botswana's light blue and black stripes are said to represent water and the zebra — both critical to the country's survival.
Angola's flag features a cogwheel and machete derived from the Soviet hammer and sickle — reflecting its Marxist independence movement.
Dominica's purple Sisserou parrot is the only national flag featuring the color purple — the parrot is critically endangered.
